title: Number of Operations to Make Network Connected
summary: Given a network of n computers connected by cables, where each computer is numbered from 0 to n-1, you can move cables between directly connected computers to connect any pair of disconnected computers.
statement: Given a network of n computers connected by cables, where each computer is numbered from 0 to n-1, you can move cables between directly connected computers to connect any pair of disconnected computers. The task is to determine the minimum number of cable movements needed to ensure all computers are connected. If it's impossible, return -1.
constraints: Computers are numbered zero through n-1 and connections are distinct undirected cables.
One operation may remove a redundant cable and reconnect two components.
Return the minimum operations to connect all computers, or -1 if there are fewer than n-1 cables.
reference_solution:
def minimum_network_operations(n,connections):
    if len(connections)<n-1:return -1
    parent=list(range(n))
    def find(node):
        while parent[node]!=node:parent[node]=parent[parent[node]];node=parent[node]
        return node
    components=n
    for left,right in connections:
        a,b=find(left),find(right)
        if a!=b:parent[a]=b;components-=1
    return components-1

hints: At least n-1 total cables are necessary.
Union endpoints while counting how many connected components remain.
If enough cables exist, every redundant cable can be moved, so return components minus one.
Joining c components requires and can be achieved with exactly c-1 replacement cables.
editorial: After the cable-count feasibility check, union-find determines the number of connected components. A graph with n nodes and c components contains enough redundant edges to join them whenever it has at least n-1 total edges, and exactly c-1 moves are necessary. The oracle independently builds adjacency lists and counts components by depth-first search.

Four cables cannot connect six computers, so the answer is minus one.
